title: PTA is one of the greatest working directors and TWBB is excellent, but Boogie Nights remains his best film in my opinion

commenti.body:
PTA is really untouchable...

If we talk about recent memory, I've always thought Inherent Vice is a masterpiece. 

I'll put it this way: There are some films while watching I felt or thought things that I haven't felt, thought before. Maybe it's atmosphere, maybe it's essence, maybe it's about it's politics, or some other stuff, I don't know, but among thousands of films I've seen, Twelve Monkeys, Come and See, Zodiac, Nights of Cabiria and Inherent Vice did it for me... 

I can't really explain it honestly, but it was just something new in everyway. And Thomas Pynchon should get a point for that.

Totally agree, that whole film is perfection. I can never get enough scenes following Burt Reynolds through the house. There’s just too much to even list. Alfred Molina? BRILLIANCE. John C. Reilly, PSH, Macy, Cheadle, Graham, Moore…everyone is amazing.
Agree, also the solemn tracking shot of him walking through the warehouse to the main theme.
That scene was so heavy after his “never video” speech earlier in the film.

Agreed. For me, post Magnolia, PTA is at his best when in comic mode. I find his comedies to be more serious work than the dramas. I also fail to love his collaborations with Day Lewis. (I'm disappointed he hasn't made another film with Joaquin Phoenix, who, it seems to me, is the perfect actor for his style.) 

Probably not a popular opinion, but for these reasons, after Inherent Vice, my favourite PTA is his last film, Licorice Pizza. Personally I thought LP was a masterful (I won't say 'a masterpiece' because I think PTA dropped the ball in the final 5 minutes). 

What both of these films share is a particular movement or feeling of unhinged reality. It's masterfully controlled, but within the control there's chaos. The world building is phenomenal. Nobody does this...  what do we call it - absurdist realism?.. like PTA. Nothing is completely serious, and yet the films are anything but trivial. You can see PTA spinning plates like a he's on-stage at Cirque De Soleil, and he makes it look so effortless I think most viewers take it for granted. I find when PTA is in this comic mode his work is absolutely thrilling. I'm aware of his talent far more when I'm watching Inherent Vice than when I'm watching TWWB.

I agree with you.  However, I consider him to be a very uneven director (just like pretty much all American directors of the 1st rank are) but he is only 53 years old and his best work may be coming.

*Note:*  Francois Truffaut made 23 feature length films, but only his first - **The 400 Blows** (France, 1959) won him Best Director at Cannes.  He never won the Palm d'Or.  He too was probably 'young, hungry, and full of creative energy' when writing and filming his first film.  Unfortunately, he ended up having a long but mediocre career.
